messages:
Maria: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector landing we saw a small regression in p95 for short prompts. Thinking the continuous-batching window parameters (micro-batch interval / coalesce delay / jitter) might need rebalancing. Anybody seen matching traces? :thinking:

Ashok: I pulled flamegraphs from canary nodes. The extra ~8–12ms at p95 looks like waiting in the coalesce queue more than kernel time. KV hit-rate also dipped ~2% in same window. Logs:```
worker.coalesce_wait_ms p95=9.8 p99=37.2
kv.cache_hit_rate 0.87 -> 0.85
kernel.exec_ms p95 no-change
```

Linh: Hmm — if coalesce delay bumped up unintentionally then token-budget gating could be firing later. We should check queue_policy changes too (we recently toggled prioritized short-request path). Can we try reducing micro-batch interval from 6ms -> 3ms and shrink jitter to +/-1ms as an experiment?

Sam: Agree with Linh on quick experiment. Note that reducing interval increases microbatch count and might hurt KV locality (more interleaving). We need to track per-run kv.hit_rate and per-token latency. Can you post the candidate config?

Linh: Candidate (quick):```json
{
  "batching": {
    "microbatch_interval_ms": 3,
    "coalesce_delay_ms": 2,
    "coalesce_jitter_ms": 1,
    "token_budget_target": 96,
    "queue_policy": "fifo_short_priority"
  }
}
```

Ashok: Will run a perf probe on a small canary with that config. Also want to try a second arm that reduces token_budget_target to 64 to see if we reduce waiting for large-token requests. Proposed A/B: A=3ms/2ms/jitter1/token96, B=3ms/2ms/jitter1/token64.

Devon: Suggest adding a third arm with slightly larger jitter to avoid synchronization: C=3ms/2ms/jitter3/token96. In past we've seen reduced p99 spikes with small jitter bumps. I'll sketch the grid:``
A: interval=3, delay=2, jitter=1, token=96
B: interval=3, delay=2, jitter=1, token=64
C: interval=3, delay=2, jitter=3, token=96
D: control (current prod params)``

Sam: Important telemetry to collect per-arm: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, kv.hit_rate, microbatch_size distribution, kernel selection breakdown, and error rates. Add trace sampling at 1% for full request traces. Also log per-request chosen kernel id to make sure kernel selector didn't change behavior under different batching.

Maria: Good. Who will run the canary and for how long? I want at least 1 hour steady-state per-arm at 3 replica nodes and traffic mirroring to avoid user impact.

Ashok: I can run it this afternoon. Plan: deploy arms to canary ring, run 1h baseline, then 1h per-arm sequentially (total ~4h). If we see clear signal earlier we can cut. I'll publish raw metrics to the perf dashboard under /dash/eng-runtime/batch-window-rebalance.

Linh: If Ashok sees KV hit-rate regress further, rollback immediately and try smaller interval change (5ms -> 4ms) instead of 6->3. We should prioritize no-drop in kv.hit_rate > 1.5%.

ci-bot: Deployment started: canary-ring v2 -> 4 nodes. Jobs: perf-probe, trace-collector. Build: runtime-3.4.1-kernel-selector

Sam: One more note — kernel scheduler uses seq-length histogram to pick kernels. If more requests are microbatched together across different seq lengths, kernel exec pattern can change and we might see micro-regen. Add seq-length bucket heatmap to the dashboard too.

Devon: I'll add a short apples-to-apples script to compute per-arm microbatch composition and kernel-switch frequency. Should help explain any exec pattern changes.

Maria: Awesome. Let's reconvene after first 2 arms. Ashok, post the dashboards link and a 2-line summary when done. Thanks :thumbsup:
